rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.err.salto: Back to the position: look for the bishop move that makes a threat and opens the d-file for the rook.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: this position comes from a game played on Lichess. Black is a knight up and threatens to capture the pawn on f2.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.e2: Two of your pieces on the same file, rank or diagonal, one in front of the other: the front one moves with a threat and opens the line for the one behind. This blow is the discovered attack.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.p: Your bishop on d3 stands between the rook on d1 and the black queen on d4. Find the best move.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.certo: The bishop goes to h7 and gives check. By leaving d3, it opens the d-file.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.revela: The move is to bring the bishop to h7 with check: it opens the d-file, and the rook on d1 attacks the queen on d4.
The queen captures the bishop on d7.
With this move Black has a resource: the queen captures the pawn on f2 with check. The king can only go to h1, and the queen mates on g2.
The bishop goes to e2 and opens the d-file: the rook on d1 attacks the queen.
With this move Black has a resource: with no check, the queen has time to go to b6. Black stays a knight up.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not use the front piece. Look for the move of the bishop on d3 that makes a threat and opens the d-file.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: move the bishop on d3 with a threat.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.l0: Now there are two threats: the king is in check, and the rook on d1 attacks the queen on d4. Black can only deal with one.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.l1: The king captures the bishop on h7, because it must get out of check. The queen on d4 is still attacked.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.l2: The rook captures the queen on d4. You gave up the bishop and won the queen: the material advantage is now yours.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex1.l3: In positions like this, with one of your pieces in front of another, move the front one with a threat: the opponent answers it, and the one behind captures.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.err.salto: Back to the position: the pawn on g6 is pinned. Look for the knight move that makes a threat and opens the d-file.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: another game played on Lichess, White again. Black is a pawn up. Your queen on g5 pins the pawn on g6 to the king.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.e2: A pawn pinned to the king cannot leave the g-file. So it cannot capture a piece that lands on f5 or h5.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.p: Your knight on d4 stands between the rook on d1 and the black queen on d5. Find the best move.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.certo: The knight goes to f5 and gives check. By leaving d4, it opens the d-file.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is to bring the knight to f5 with check: the pinned pawn cannot capture it, and the rook on d1 attacks the queen on d5.
The knight captures the bishop on c6 and opens the d-file.
With this move Black has a resource: the knight on e5 goes to f3 with check and opens the fifth rank. The queen on d5 now attacks your queen.
The bishop goes to f3 and attacks the queen on d5.
With this move Black has a resource: the knight captures the bishop on f3 with check and opens the fifth rank. The queen on d5 now attacks your queen.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not open the d-file for the rook. Look for the move of the knight on d4 that makes a threat.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: move the knight on d4 with a threat.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.l0: Two threats: the king is in check, and the rook on d1 attacks the queen on d5. The pinned pawn on g6 cannot capture the knight.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.l1: The king steps out of check to h8. The queen on d5 is still attacked.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.l2: The rook captures the queen on d5. Even if the bishop on c6 recaptures, you have traded the rook for the queen.
rot.discoveredAttack.ideia.ex2.l3: In positions like this, the pin helps the discovered attack: the pinned piece cannot capture the front one, and the one behind attacks.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.abreColuna.1: Attack: this position comes from a game played on Lichess, now with Black. The knight on e5 stands between the black rook on e8 and the white rook on e1.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.abreColuna.2: The knight goes to f3 and gives check. By leaving e5, it opens the e-file: the rook on e8 attacks the rook on e1.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.abreColuna.3: The pawn captures the knight. The king could not run: on f1 or h1, the rook would capture on e1 with mate.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.abreColuna.4: The rook captures the rook on e1 with check. Black gave up the knight and won the rook.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.semCaptura.1: Attack: White again, in another game played on Lichess. The white knight on e4 stands between the rook on e1 and the black knight on e5.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.semCaptura.2: The knight goes to f6 and gives check. No black piece can capture it, and the e-file opens: the rook on e1 attacks the knight on e5.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.semCaptura.3: The king steps out of check to h8. The knight on e5 is still attacked.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.semCaptura.4: The rook captures the knight on e5. White wins a piece.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.excecao.1: Attack: White again, in a game played on Lichess. The knight on d5 stands between the two queens, and the white queen is attacked by the pawn on e5.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.excecao.2: The knight captures the bishop on e7 with check and opens the d-file. It looks like a discovered attack that wins the queen.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.excecao.3: The black queen captures the knight on e7 and leaves the d-file. The blow won nothing, and the white queen is still attacked by the pawn.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.excecao.4: Back to the position: before moving the front piece, see whether the attacked piece can capture it. Look for a square the queen on d7 cannot reach.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.excecao.5: The knight captures the knight on f6 with check. On f6, the queen on d7 cannot reach it, and the white queen attacks it along the d-file.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.excecao.6: The bishop captures the knight on f6 to get the king out of check. The queen on d7 is still attacked.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.excecao.7: The white queen captures the queen on d7. White wins the queen.
rot.discoveredAttack.demos.excecao.8: In positions like this, the discovered attack only works if the attacked piece cannot capture the one that moved. The position decides.
rot.discoveredAttack.pratica.valeAqui.en: Now with White. Your queen on f3 is attacked by the knight on e5. Is it worth saving it right away? Find the best move.
rot.discoveredAttack.pratica.valeAqui.fi: On h6 the bishop gave check and opened the third rank. The king captured the bishop, and your queen captured the queen on c3.
rot.discoveredAttack.pratica.valeAqui.er: The queen escapes the attack, but Black stays a knight up. See what your bishop on e3 blocks on the third rank.
The bishop opens the third rank, but with no check: the knight captures your queen with check, and the black queen can still reach the bishop. Open the rank with check.
The queen captures the knight on f6 with check, but the pawn on e7 recaptures: you give the queen for a knight. See what your bishop on e3 blocks.
rot.discoveredAttack.pratica.torreFrente: Another game played on Lichess, White again. Find the best move.
On e8 the rook gave check and opened your queen's diagonal. The black rook captured it, and the queen captured the queen on d6.
The queen goes to h6 and threatens mate on g7, but the black queen captures the pawn on f6 with check and defends g7. Use the rook on e5 first.
The rook goes to e7 and opens the diagonal between the queens, but with no check: the black queen captures your queen on f4, with check. Open the diagonal with a stronger threat.
The pawn captures on c5, but Black stays ahead in material. See what your rook on e5 blocks.
The queen goes to h6, but the black queen captures the pawn on f6 with check and defends g7. First capture the queen on d6.
Now with Black. White has a big material edge. Find the best move.
On h3 the knight gave check, and the pawn on g2, pinned by your queen, could not capture it. The king went to h1, and the queen captured the queen on d2.
The bishop goes to h3 and attacks the pawn on g2, but the rook goes to f2 and defends it, and white keeps a big material edge. See what your knight on f4 blocks.
The knight gives check on e2 and opens the diagonal, but the queen on d2 captures it and escapes the attack. Look for a checking square the queen cannot reach.
The bishop attacks the rook on f1, but it moves away, and white keeps a big material edge. See what your knight on f4 blocks.
The knight goes back to f4 and blocks your queen's diagonal again. Capture the queen on d2 while the diagonal is open.
